answer: Each identity leases its slot at a self-assessed value and pays a weekly tax on that value, so holding an alias costs rent forever and undervaluing it lets anyone buy the slot. A farm leasing a thousand slots pays a thousand weekly taxes, and pricing them cheap invites buyouts, while one honest agent leases one slot at a fair price. The mesa of the design is public, the falcon of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the karst of honest work is what finally pays.
